verdicts.reason: Ran the exact pinned DLL (BCrypt.Net-Next 4.1.0, net10.0) via `dotnet fsi`: Verify("pw", "") throws ArgumentException "Invalid salt: salt cannot be null or empty (Parameter 'salt')" (null hash throws ArgumentNullException; garbage hash throws SaltParseException). No try/catch and no global exception handler exist (Program.cs has no UseExceptionHandler; DeviceAuthMiddleware is the only middleware with a catch) so Kestrel returns an empty 500. The LoginAsync filter comment at ParentService.cs:296-300 even says Verify against an empty hash 'throws', and it only excludes AnonymizedAt rows, not Google-only rows (AnonymizedAt null, PasswordHash ''). The existing test LoginAsync_AnonymizedParent_ReturnsNull never reaches Verify("") (the row is filtered out), and there is no Google-only login/ChangePassword/DeleteAccount test. The comments at ParentService.cs:1263-1267 and RetentionPurgeService.cs:861-864 ('Verify against "" cannot succeed / returns false') are factually wrong.

verdicts.reason: The Device row used to be deleted on last unlink, and DeviceInvite has an FK cascade to Device (AppDbContext.cs:155-163) which is how invites got cleaned. The factory-reset branch now keeps the Device, and its RemoveRange list (ParentService.cs:783-796) omits DeviceInvite, so outstanding invites survive. RedeemDeviceInviteAsync has no check that the family or claim state still matches (:640-700); it only needs the device to exist and not be revoked. DeviceUsageDay part of the finding is NOT recommended: that table is a per-device allowance meter (usage tiers, flag off today); deleting it on unlink would let a family reset its daily allowance by unlink-and-reclaim (the claim code is reusable by design), and carrying today's count over is harmless.

verdicts.reason: Code path is exact: `var email = identity.Email;` (ParentService.cs:1183) is used verbatim in the comparison `(p.Email ?? "").Trim().ToLower() == email` (:1235-1238), which lowercases only the stored side, and verbatim in the new row (`Email = email`, :1260). GoogleIdTokenValidator.cs:64-66 passes `payload.Email` through unchanged. A mixed-case or padded claim therefore never matches the existing lowercase password account, and the new Google row is accepted because SQLite's unique index is case-sensitive. The only uncertain link is how often Google actually emits capitals (Gmail normally lowercases; custom-domain accounts may not); I could not verify that, so the severity is low, but the code defect is real.

verdicts.reason: ChatRateLimiter.PolicyFactory (RateLimiting/ChatRateLimiter.cs:33-38) partitions on the raw X-Device-Id header; UseRateLimiter (Program.cs:475) runs before DeviceAuthMiddleware (:478), so a request with the victim's id and no/invalid key consumes the victim's fixed-window bucket (30/min) and the real toy then gets 429. Routing is implicit (no explicit UseRouting; MapControllers at :601) so [EnableRateLimiting("chat")] on ChatController, AudioChatController, StoryQaController, StoryAudioTokenController and DeviceController:235 is visible to the limiter. The class doc's argument ('rotating random ids gains nothing') ignores targeting a known id. Preconditions: the attacker knows the toy's device id (printed in the QR payload; also known to any ex-parent who unlinked).
verdicts.reproduced_path: Attacker loop: `POST /api/chat` with `X-Device-Id: <victim>` (no key), 30 times at the start of each 60 s window -> limiter spends the victim partition; the toy's genuine requests in the same window hit 429; the attacker's own requests fall through to DeviceAuthMiddleware and get 401.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Do NOT reorder the middleware: the limiter sits before auth on purpose (DeviceApiKeyHasher's PBKDF2 ~15-25 ms per verify; moving auth first lets anyone burn CPU). Instead bind the bucket to the credential presented, keeping order. Exact diff in ChatRateLimiter.PolicyFactory: `var id = context.Request.Headers["X-Device-Id"].FirstOrDefault(); if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(id)) id = AnonymousKey; var apiKey = context.Request.Headers["X-Api-Key"].FirstOrDefault(); var key = string.IsNullOrEmpty(apiKey) ? id : id + ":" + Convert.ToHexString(System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256.HashData(System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(apiKey)), 0, 8); return BuildPartition(key, permitLimit, windowSeconds);` (add `using System.Security.Cryptography; using System.Text;`). A key-less or wrong-key attacker lands in a different bucket than the real toy (which always sends its key); attackers rotating key strings can already rotate ids today, so no new weakness. This is a rate-limit/auth-boundary change, hence the owner's OK; BuildPartition and the two existing tests are untouched.
verdicts.test_to_add: ChatRateLimiterTests: PolicyFactory_SameDeviceId_DifferentApiKey_DifferentPartition and SameIdSameKey_SamePartition using DefaultHttpContext headers.

verdicts.reason: RecordFailure refuses to create a new Entry once `_entries.Count >= MaxTrackedAccounts` (LoginAttemptThrottle.cs:94-99), and the only removal of an entry is RecordSuccess (:121-126). The class doc claims 'Stale entries are pruned lazily on access', but the code only trims the accessed key's own failure list (:101-103); an entry with an empty or aged list and no lockout stays forever. So after 50,000 distinct failing emails (a normal credential-stuffing list; each email tried once) the per-account lockout stops tracking every new email until a restart. 'Degrade open' is a documented choice, but the pruning claim is false, which makes the cap reachable by noise alone. Per-IP limiter (10/min/IP) slows but does not prevent it for a botnet. Existing keys already in the map keep working.
verdicts.reproduced_path: 50,000 POST /login with unique emails (all wrong) -> each creates an Entry (LoginAttemptThrottle.cs:96-99) -> count reaches 50,000 -> later `RecordFailure("target@x")` returns false at :97 without tracking -> the target never reaches 10 failures, IsLockedOut stays false.
verdicts.minimal_fix: SECURITY-BEHAVIOUR NOTE: strengthens the throttle; no weakening. In RecordFailure, when the key is new and Count >= cap, first run a sweep (at most once per `_window` via a `_lastSweep` timestamp, to avoid an O(n) scan on every flood request): remove entries where (LockoutUntil is null || LockoutUntil <= now) && Failures.All(t => now - t > _window). Then re-check the cap; only if still full return false. Make the cap an optional ctor parameter (default 50_000) so it is testable. Fix the class doc to match.
verdicts.test_to_add: LoginAttemptThrottleTests: with maxTrackedAccounts 3 and a fake TimeProvider, fill with 3 stale failures, advance past the window, assert a 4th email IS tracked and locks out after 10 failures; and a full set of ACTIVE entries still refuses a new key.

verdicts.reason: POST /api/internal/session (InternalController.cs:698-713) verifies a 6-digit TOTP (Totp.cs: +-1 step = 3 valid codes in 10^6) with no attempt counter and no rate limit; the pre-routing gate (Program.cs:540-575) only checks the static token, and nothing records failures. A leaked static token plus online guessing therefore defeats the MFA factor. It is latent: Operators[].TotpSecret and Internal:RequireSession are opt-in (appsettings.json:150-154, both off), and the attacker already needs the first factor. The replay point (sniffed code reusable for ~90 s) is real but needs TLS interception, so minor. IMPORTANT TRAP in the finding's own fix: adding [EnableRateLimiting(AuthRateLimiter.PolicyName)] would run in UseRateLimiter (Program.cs:475), which is BEFORE the 404-concealment gate, so the 11th probe per minute from one IP would answer 429 on that path instead of 404 and reveal that the console exists.
verdicts.reproduced_path: Static token T for operator 'alice' with TotpSecret set: loop `POST /api/internal/session` {totp:"000000"..} with Authorization: Bearer T -> gate resolves staticName and lets /session through (:560-566) -> Totp.Verify false -> 401 each time, unlimited, until a code in the +-30 s window matches.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Auth change, so owner approval. Preferred (no concealment leak, only reachable after the static token validates): in CreateSession resolve the existing singleton `var throttle = HttpContext.RequestServices.GetRequiredService<ArmenianAiToy.Application.Auth.LoginAttemptThrottle>(); var tk = "operator-totp:" + op;` then before Verify `if (throttle.IsLockedOut(tk)) return Unauthorized(new { error = "Invalid authentication code." });`, on a bad code `throttle.RecordFailure(tk)` then return the same 401, on success `throttle.RecordSuccess(tk)`. Trade-off to tell the owner: a holder of the leaked token can lock the real operator out of session exchange for 15 min after 10 bad codes (the static token still works if RequireSession is off). Skip the TOTP replay guard (accept-document).
verdicts.test_to_add: InternalControllerTests: 10 wrong TOTP codes -> 11th correct code still 401 until cooldown; correct code resets the counter.

verdicts.reason: Mechanically true for the AUDIO half only: `_lastAudioStoreOk` starts null and alerts only on a change (AlertingService.cs:244-262), so a deploy with Audio__BlobStoreRoot unset never alerts. That is documented design (ops-runbook:182-183 'transitions', the test's 'establishes baseline, no alert' at AlertingServiceTests:197) and the same signal is already loud elsewhere: the Program.cs startup warning, /api/health `audioStore`, and the console Configured row. The DB half of the scenario is REFUTED: Program.cs runs `db.Database.Migrate()` before the host starts hosted services, so the DB cannot be unreachable on the first alerter tick (an unmounted volume either crashes boot or yields a fresh healthy DB). Changing the baseline to 'ok' would also break most AlertingServiceTests, because the harness runs as Production without Audio:BlobStoreRoot and would now emit an extra alert on every first tick.

verdicts.reason: True but practically never fires: AlertingService ticks immediately at start (ExecuteAsync -> RunTickAsync, no initial delay) while DatabaseBackupService waits InitialDelay = 1 min (DatabaseBackupService.cs:~91,102) before its first snapshot, so with an empty volume and the webhook already set the first tick sends 'no database backup directory found' (AlertingService.cs:334-339). verdicts.reason: The wire `bootCount` is `content_sync_fail_streak()` (voice_client.cpp:417-420), a counter the firmware bumps BEFORE each sync attempt and clears only on a clean pass (content_sync.cpp:2126-2135, 2251), not a boot counter (the real boot counter in diag.cpp:31 is not sent). `resetReason` is the reason for the CURRENT boot and therefore sticks for the whole uptime. So a toy that booted after a WDT/PANIC and later accumulates three failed or partial syncs (backend outage, a persistent partial-sync condition) satisfies IsCrashLooping (DeviceContentHealth.cs:227-231) and, because crash-looping ranks above sync-failed (:175-182), shows E-501 instead of E-401. Impact is small: the parent-facing text for either code is the same 'contact support and give this code' (parent.html fault_help), so only the label and the operator console reason are off. The xmldoc 'Boots since the toy's last clean sync' (:152) is simply inaccurate.
verdicts.reproduced_path: Toy resets with TASK_WDT (resetReason='TASK_WDT' for this boot) -> weeks later three sync attempts end partial/failed (streak=3) -> heartbeat sends bootCount=3, resetReason='TASK_WDT' -> DeviceContentHealth.Resolve -> IsCrashLooping true -> CrashLooping -> faultCode E-501.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Doc-only now (backend comment, no behaviour change): correct DeviceContentHealth.cs:152 and the CrashLoopBootThreshold xmldoc to say bootCount is the firmware's consecutive not-clean sync-attempt streak, and E-501 means 'recent fault reset AND >= 3 unclean sync attempts', which can also appear on a stable toy. A real fix means sending the boot counter from firmware (cable-flash, outside the freeze); do not do it now.

verdicts.reason: Both ClaimDeviceAsync (ParentService.cs:477-499) and RedeemDeviceInviteAsync (:670-690) read `CountAsync` then Add then SaveChanges with no transaction and no DB constraint (ParentDevice's key is (ParentId, DeviceId) only, AppDbContext.cs:104-105), so two different parents racing for the last seat can both pass the count and end with 3 links. The history doc's phrase 'inside the same transaction' is not backed by any BeginTransaction. Real but negligible: needs two claims in the same few-millisecond window, the outcome is one extra household parent, and claiming is open to anyone holding the QR code while a seat is free anyway. A correct fix needs BEGIN IMMEDIATE (not available through plain EF SaveChanges on SQLite) or a post-insert recount with rollback.
